_README: Curated laws for ds_contract, merged onto the primitive it names. Absence of an entry means nobody has written the law yet — NOT that anything is permitted. Keep this small: a rule here is a rule an agent will follow, and a stale one is worse than none. Every entry cites where the decision was taken. A key here is a COMPONENT ID — overrides merge onto the inventory walk by id, so an entry named after a token constant (KIOSK_UTILITY_SHEET) merges onto nothing and is law no agent can find. A token's law lives in its docblock, which ds_tokens serves as the `use` sentence on that axis.

ContextualSidebar.useWhen: left sidebar, page sidebar, contextual sidebar, per-page nav, Vercel sidebar, lane door, parent nav vs child nav, back row, views list, sidebar filters, where do a page's views go, outbound sidebar, morph sidebar, sidebar mode, mode switcher, FBA mode, label intake mode, sidebar category heading, hairline divider, sidebar head order, sidebar top layout, where does the back button go, back button below search, find above back, page modes below back button, sidebar header stacking order, chat sidebar, chat threads in the sidebar, recent sessions, new chat button, view-less page panel
ContextualSidebar.doNot: Do not list a lane's pages or a page's views in the page map (parent nav) once that lane is a door — no dropdown, no child rows; the lane is ONE row that opens its landing page. Do not put a page's verbs (Sync, Export, Add) in the sidebar — they sit in the desk header, top-right over the list they act on (NavPageActions); the one exception is a VIEW-LESS panel whose recents list IS the sidebar (Chat, `NAV_PAGE_DECLS[...].recentsPanel`), where the verbs ride the `‹` back row as glyph buttons (NavPanelActions, chord keycap on hover). Do not give a page its own sidebar component or row renderer — it DECLARES data (NAV_PAGE_DECLS, the recents surface registry) and the host paints it. Do not add a second search field: the pinned top row is the ONE field (NavFind) on every page — scoped to the page's list on a panel, the ⌘K palette's face elsewhere. Do not paint a page's views as body rows: they live behind the head's view switcher. Do not put saved views or filters behind a menu: they are the body's buttons. Do not reorder the head: the search field is never below `‹`, `‹` is never below the mode switcher, the mode switcher is never below the view switcher, and nothing (views, filters, page verbs) is inserted between them. Do not repeat the account / sign-in footer under every page panel; it lives on the page map.
ContextualSidebar.law: src/components/sidebar/contextual/ContextualSidebar.tsx. SIDEBAR HEAD ORDER (operator 2026-09-27, every page panel, top → bottom, all pinned): 1) collapse · THE search field (NavFind: the page's list on a panel with a list — narrows it, grows right over the header while focused, locate pills under it — else the ⌘K everywhere face) — paste-a-list status rides directly right of it; 2) `‹ <Lane/Page>` back row; 3) the MODE switcher (NavModeSwitcher, lane door landing pages only); 4) the VIEW switcher (NavViewSwitcher). Both are NavSwitcherMenu blocks (operator 2026-09-27: modes and views change rarely, so they sit behind one block each that opens to the RIGHT of the sidebar on hover). The body starts BELOW them with what changes often, as buttons: saved views, then filters. A slot that has no data is omitted without reordering the rest; after `‹` (the page map peek) the field stays pinned in the same place. ONE HOST (operator 2026-09-27): it is the desktop sidebar on EVERY page — a page with `rollout: contextual` gets its own panel, every other page (legacy rollout, scan stations) gets the page map with the page lit; never mount MasterNav/DashboardSidebar in the desktop column (it survives only in the phone-width drawer). LANE DOOR pattern (operator 2026-09-27): parent = the page map, one row per lane (`LANE_DOORS` in src/lib/nav/lanes.ts names the landing page; legacy spine SidebarNavList.renderLane and the resolver laneMap both honour it). Child = the landing page's contextual sidebar: pinned head (collapse · the search field, then `‹ <Lane>`), then the MODE switcher (NavModeSwitcher: the lane's pages as modes — Outbound = Shipping · FBA · Label intake; the resolver emits them as the `<page>.<lane>.modes` section), then the VIEW switcher (NavViewSwitcher: current view's glyph · label · count; the menu lists every view with NAV_VIEW_ICONS glyph, digit key, count). Body: the view's saved views FIRST as one-click preset blocks (Bookmark glyph, lit plate when the URL matches, hover × delete, `Save view` block only while unsaved filters are on; nothing when neither) — pinned at the top as buttons, never behind a menu — then NavFilters: a Sort row (the list's order; queues default to ship-by, soonest first), one row per staff ROLE (Assigned / Picked by / Packer / Tester on queues; Staff / Picked by / Packed by / Tested by on Shipped), one row per date range (Ship by, Ordered; Shipped with a time of day at each end), then the facet rows (closed rows, value chip, Reset pill riding the category hairline — Reset clears filters, never the sort; open options with count 0 sink to the end dimmed unless selected). All of it declared as NavControls (staff[], dateRanges[], sort) in NAV_PAGE_DECLS; every control param must be declared on its route and narrow the facet counts too. Categories are separated by hairlines, never text headings — map and panel alike. Page map order: top rows, lanes, Automations, Scan Stations LAST. Map ↔ contextual swap morphs in DesktopRouteShell (directional blur-slide, sidebarScopeSwap timing). The server contract (`GET /api/nav/context`) carries all of it, so Tauri gets the same IA. CHAT (operator 2026-09-27): Chat is the FIRST row of the page map and the ⌘K pin. `/ai-chat` is a view-less `recentsPanel` page: head = the search field over Chat's list ('Find chats', desk store, narrows the threads) · `‹ Chat`; `‹ Chat …… [+]` — New chat rides the back row (NavPanelActions, intent `ai-chat:new` registered by the page; hover discloses its ⌘⇧O / Ctrl+Shift+O keycaps — ⌘N is Chrome's new window, never advertised); body = its threads through NavRecentsList (`assistant.sessions`, ⌥1…⌥0 open the first ten). ACCOUNT FOOTER (operator 2026-09-27): the staff account bar (StaffAccountFooter) renders at the PARENT level only — the page map (legacy pages, and a panel's `‹` peek) — never under a page's own contextual panel.

NavFind.useWhen: global search, command K, Ctrl K, ⌘K button, find in this list, F to find, page search, table search in the sidebar, search hotkey, find button position, one search field, search scope, scope chip, search everywhere, merge search bars, two search fields, where is this order, which view holds it, locate pills, search overflow, search wider than the sidebar, paste many order numbers anywhere
NavFind.doNot: Do not mount a second search field in the sidebar or header — there is ONE (NavFind). Do not paint the scope inside the field (no chip): the view switcher under it already names the list, and the field's width belongs to the operator's words. Do not clip the operator's text to the sidebar: while focused the page field grows RIGHT over the header (FindField overflowRight) — its 32px slot never moves anything. Do not open the palette as the page field is typed into (the list narrows live). Do not count a locate pill with a predicate its list does not use. Do not route scans or identify lookups through the page field — that is the palette's job. Do not write the desk-store Find to the URL. Do not mount a page field in the header while the sidebar is closed: the table bar's Find owns the list then. Do not put the keycap at the far right or after the words.
NavFind.law: src/components/sidebar/contextual/NavFind.tsx (operator 2026-09-27). ONE field, search split by the ANSWER: PAGE = narrow the list on screen (`search.source` desk-store / url-param; bare `F` focuses; FindField overflowRight: while focused the well grows right to max(slot, 28rem) over the header's task/pin keys, z-50, the slot keeps 32px); CONTEXTUAL = where the text lives in the section — `search.locate` declares a locator, `GET /api/nav/locate?locator=&q=` answers per-bucket counts with each bucket list's OWN predicate, painted as pills in the panel under the field (tone dot · label · count, the list on screen pressed in, click = that bucket's href with the text kept as its desk Find), and a pasted list of 2+ numbers becomes the located list (NavBulkList); GLOBAL = the ⌘K palette: 'Search everywhere for “…”' row / ⌘↵ / Ctrl+↵ (openCommandBar({ query, scope: 'everywhere' }), CommandBarOpenDetail in app-events.ts; CommandBar.tsx belongs to the search session). With no list (identify, page map, header) the field is the palette's face (RollingHint 'Search' …, ⌘K keycaps, paste key); a paste of 2+ numbers there is located EVERYWHERE (useLocalBulkList('everywhere')), anything else opens the palette already searching. Order inside the well: glyph → keycap → words (HOTKEY FIRST).

FindField.useWhen: find field, search field, search box, search bar, find bar, table search, data table find, find in this list, F to find, search placeholder animation, rolling placeholder, rotating hint text, animated placeholder, hint roll, text switching animation, paste button in search, paste to find, ⌘K face words, hover to reveal what a search does
FindField.doNot: Do not hand-roll a search input with its own draft/debounce, keycap, clear and placeholder — mount FindField. Do not animate a hint on page load or loop it while nobody is looking: it RESTS on its first phrase and rolls only on hover or focus. Do not change the timing outside the preset (0.22s spring, 1.8s hold, 180ms hover intent) — hover-only means brisk but readable. No bounce/overshoot and no blur on the roll. Do not use a native placeholder for the hint. Do not split the hint into per-word animation — the phrase rolls as one line.
FindField.law: src/design-system/components/FindField.tsx (operator 2026-09-27). ONE find well for every list: the sidebar search field in its page scope (NavFind), the data-table bar Find when the sidebar is closed (TriageSelectBar BarFind), and any future table find. Anatomy left → right: Search glyph · `F` keycap · field · clear (only with text) · paste key (ClipboardPaste, far right; reads the clipboard through the same paste door as ⌘V). At rest the hint is gray and the keycap and paste key are hidden (keycap takes no room); while looked at (hover / focus) the hint turns black and both show — `findHintTone`, `HoverKeycaps`, `PasteKey`, exported with `findWellClass` so the everywhere face wears the same parts (operator 2026-09-27). Optional `escalate(query)` + `below` (ReactNode) fill a panel hung under the well while it has focus and text (below first, then the 'Search everywhere' row with ⌘↵ keycaps first). Optional `overflowRight`: the well leaves its 32px slot and grows right while focused (focus-within:w-[max(100%,28rem)], z-50) — the operator's words outrank the layout; the slot holds the space so nothing moves. HINT = RollingHint: rests on its first phrase ('Find' / ⌘K 'Search'); while the operator looks at it (pointer over it, or focus — `F`, a click; `useHintActivity`) the later phrases roll top → bottom ONE LINE AT A TIME (operator 2026-09-27: per line, never per word — read in one glance; motionPresence.findHintRoll on the whole phrase: opacity + y inside a soft masked edge, no blur; motionTransition.findHintRoll = critically damped spring, visualDuration 0.22s, bounce 0). Hover intent 180ms (a pointer passing through never rolls), then 1.8s per phrase. Leaving rolls back to the rest phrase; the next look resumes at the phrase after the last one shown. `findHints(label)` = ['Find', the list's 'Find …', 'Paste to find']. NavFind's everywhere face uses the same RollingHint + useHintActivity. Reduced motion keeps the swap, drops slide and blur. Sizes: `sidebar` (6px corner, caption) and `bar` (8px corner, body).

NavModeSwitcher.useWhen: sidebar mode switcher, page modes, lane modes, Shipping FBA Label intake switch, mode dropdown under the back button, where do a lane's pages go on its landing page
NavModeSwitcher.doNot: Do not render modes as rows in the body or above `‹`. Do not give a lane of one reachable page a switcher (one page is no choice). Do not add counts to a mode.
NavModeSwitcher.law: src/components/sidebar/contextual/NavModeSwitcher.tsx on NavSwitcherMenu. One block pinned in the sidebar head DIRECTLY BELOW the `‹ <Lane>` back row and above the view switcher (see ContextualSidebar SIDEBAR HEAD ORDER). PARENT tier (see NavSwitcherMenu TWO TIERS). It names the mode you are in; hover or Enter opens the lane's other pages to the right of the sidebar; the resolver emits them as the `<page>.<lane>.modes` section (operator 2026-09-27).

NavSwitcherMenu.useWhen: sidebar views dropdown, view switcher, mode switcher, Exceptions PO paired Pick list To ship Shipped switch, Shipping FBA Label intake switch, view hotkey, 1-9 view switch, digit keycap in a menu, view count, view total chip, exceptions alert count, hover menu to the right of the sidebar, flyout beside the sidebar, progressive disclosure of hotkeys, parent vs child nav, parent level button, which one is the parent, G then S, go keys
NavSwitcherMenu.doNot: Do not open a sidebar menu downward over the column or let it overlap the sidebar — it opens to the RIGHT, starting at the column's edge, so the pointer can travel the sidebar freely. Do not make it modal. Do not paint hotkeys on the closed block — keys are taught in the open menu. Do not fork the hover timing: useHoverSurface (0ms open, 150ms close). Do not hover-open while a field has focus (the menu would take it from Find). Do not derive a view count from the filtered facets query. Do not mark the current choice with a check or a dark outline — press it into the surface. Do not slide keys in front of a menu label (the text moves); fade them in at the far right. Do not paint a row's keys at rest, even inside the open menu. Do not put the parent's icon in a dark tile — the raised card, weight and ⇅ carry the tier.
NavSwitcherMenu.law: src/components/sidebar/contextual/NavSwitcherMenu.tsx (operator 2026-09-27). ONE switcher for things changed rarely: the lane MODE (NavModeSwitcher) and the page VIEW (NavViewSwitcher). At rest: one NAV_BLOCK_CLASS block (32px, hairline ring) naming the current choice — glyph · label · (views) its unfiltered count chip · ChevronRight. Radix DropdownMenu, modal=false, side=right, align=start, sideOffset = sidebar column right − block right; opens on mouse hover through useHoverSurface or Enter/Space/↓ (an open menu takes focus, so hover never opens it while an editable field — Find — has focus). Menu rows: glyph → label → count chip → keys (far right, Linear-style menu shortcut). The current choice sits PRESSED into the surface — NAV_CHOICE_SELECTED_CLASS (bg-surface-sunken + soft inset shade + hairline, the Find well), never a check (reads as multi-select) and never a hard dark outline; every choice row sinks 1px while pressed (NAV_CHOICE_PRESS_CLASS). Keys (views: bare 1–9 on VIEW_HOTKEY_PAGES: outbound, painted order, ignored in editable targets / with modifiers / when defaultPrevented, live whether or not the menu is open; modes: `G` then letter) hold their column width always and only FADE in while the row is hovered or keyboard-highlighted (Radix data-highlighted) — the label never moves. (Sliding HoverKeycaps stays for the Find / ⌘K wells only.) Categories split by DropdownMenuSeparator, never a heading. VIEW COUNTS: SIDEBAR_CHIP_CORNER tabular-nums chip rolling via AnimatedStat speed=fast — the view's UNFILTERED total from `GET /api/nav/facets?context=<pageId.viewId>&<the view href's own params>` `total` (react-query, shared key with NavFilters, 20s stale); a view with no facet context paints no chip; amber for an `alertCount` view (Exceptions) while > 0. ALERT BEACON: while another view's `alertCount` total is > 0, the closed block carries it as an amber glyph+count chip (and in its aria-label), so an at-rest operator still sees Exceptions without opening the menu. One choice is no choice: nothing renders. TWO TIERS (operator 2026-09-27), told apart before reading: PARENT (`kind=mode`, a place) = raised card at rest (bg-surface-card + shadow-sm + ring-border-soft, h-9), the lane icon plain in full ink (operator 2026-09-27: no dark tile), semibold, ChevronsUpDown ⇅, keys `G` then a letter; CHILD (`kind=view`, a list in that place) = hairline block (h-8), the bare state glyph, medium, count chip, ChevronRight ›, bare `1`–`9`.

NavFilters.useWhen: sidebar filters, triage controls, staff role filter, picked by filter, packer filter, date range filter, ship-by date, order date, shipped time of day, sort in the sidebar, saved views buttons, reset filters
NavFilters.doNot: Do not put what the operator changes often behind a menu. Do not count or Reset the sort — it is view state, not a filter. Do not mark a single choice (sort) with a check. Do not declare a control whose param the list and its facet counts do not both apply. Do not re-declare a control shape per page in the component — declare NavControls in NAV_PAGE_DECLS.
NavFilters.law: src/components/sidebar/contextual/NavFilters.tsx (operator 2026-09-27). The body is buttons, top → bottom: saved views; the Reset hairline (count + Reset clear FILTERS only); Sort (single choice pressed in, NAV_CHOICE_SELECTED_CLASS); one row per staff ROLE (`controls.staff[]`, StageStaffAssignPopover); one row per date range (`controls.dateRanges[]`, DateRangePickerField compact; a range with fromTimeParam/toTimeParam adds HH:mm fields once dates are set); then the facet rows (multi-select checkboxes with counts). Every control param comes from navControlParams(), must be declared on the view's route, and must narrow the list and its facet counts through the same server builder (sqlDeskRefinementClauses / buildPackerLogBaseWhere).

NavGoKeys.useWhen: G then letter, go to shortcut, leader key, sequence shortcut, Linear style navigation keys, G S shipping, G F FBA, G L label intake, jump to a mode, parent level hotkeys
NavGoKeys.doNot: Do not bind modes to Ctrl/Alt+digit (Chrome on Linux switches tabs; ⌥1…⌥0 are chat recents) or to bare digits (views own 1–9). Do not arm inside a text field, on a key repeat, with ⌘/Ctrl/Alt, or from a scanner burst (< 30ms between keys). Do not offer a letter for a page the staffer lacks `requires` for. Do not cache targets in session state — derive them from the registry.
NavGoKeys.law: src/components/sidebar/contextual/NavGoKeys.tsx + src/lib/keyboard/go-keys.ts (pure machine, tested) + src/lib/nav/go-keys.ts (NAV_GO_PAGES, keyed by letter so no two pages share one). Tap `G`, release, tap the letter within 1500ms: `G S` Shipping, `G F` FBA, `G L` Label intake, from ANY desk page. Targets are static: getSidebarPageNav(pageId) gated by the page's `requires` permission (the resolver's own gate), Shipping via useLaneDoorHref (last view). Mounted once by ContextualSidebar. While armed a card flush to the sidebar's right edge (level with the mode switcher) lists every letter; Escape / pointerdown / timeout disarm. The `?` and ⌘⇧? / Ctrl+Shift+? cheat sheet (KeyboardShortcutsCheatSheet) lists the go keys and the page's view digits while they are mounted (registerShortcutOverviewGroup).

NavBulkList.useWhen: paste a list, bulk paste, many order numbers, many tracking numbers, vendor list, reconcile deliveries, received vs not received, where do these numbers live, check receipts, bulk lookup in Find, pasted list popout, status chips above the deliveries, paste a list in the global search
NavBulkList.doNot: Do not write a pasted multi-number list into the desk store or the Find text — it becomes `search.locate.param` in the URL (or component state on the everywhere face). Do not give the popout its own lookup or verdict: every row, chip and count comes from ONE locator answer (`useNavLocate(scope, { refs })` → GET /api/nav/locate), whose bucket membership is the same predicate the bucket's list uses; inbound bucket ids stay the recon statuses (`received` / `not_received`) so the ledger's `?recon=` filter (`filterRowsByRecon`) and the popout agree. Do not special-case a locator in the popout (no `STATUS_FACE`, `RECON_STATUS_LABELS`, `applyInboundLane`): a number in a bucket that is not the list on screen carries a link chip to that bucket's href, narrowed by its desk Find — that is how Exceptions is reached. Do not paint a bucket with a raw hue; ink comes from `NAV_LOCATE_TONE_VAR` (nav-locate-tone.ts) keyed by `NAV_LOCATE_TONES`. Do not round the popout past rounded-sm or give rows a square hover; rows hover as an inset pill. Do not ship a row verb without its keycap in the footer legend.
NavBulkList.law: src/components/sidebar/contextual/NavBulkList.tsx + NavBulkPopout.tsx over `NavLocateResponse` (src/lib/nav/context/schema.ts); ref parsing from src/lib/receiving/reconcile.ts (`parseRefList` / `parseRefInParam` / `serializeRefIn`). Declared per view as `NavSearch.locate` (`{ locator: 'inbound', param: 'ref_in', statusParam: 'recon' }`, pages.ts → incoming.pipeline) and read by `useNavBulkList(locate)` (URL-backed); the global face uses `useLocalBulkList('everywhere')` (component state, no page list, bucket ids `<locator>:<id>`). Find's onPaste: `BulkList.paste(text)` takes 2+ numbers (newline/comma/semicolon/tab, cap 100) → the list; one number stays a Find; typed `A, B` + Enter too. Right of the well: `[›] [B] N` toggle (bare B, ↓ from Find) opens a right-start Popover, rounded-sm, h-8 sort bar (Pasted · [O] Order ID ↑↓ · [S] Status = bucket order, found-nowhere first · copy shown · clear), then a bucket filter row (All N · each bucket with its count · Not found N) writing `statusParam`. Rows: bucket glyph + label chip in the bucket's tone (or Not found) → number (mono) → detail → title → link chips to its other buckets; hover/cursor = inset pill, press sinks 1px; row verbs Open record (when `recordHref`)/Edit/Copy/Remove (E · C · ⌫). ↵ pinpoints: when a bucket holding the number is the list on screen (href pathname + view params match, or a verdict bucket with no href), the desk Find narrows to it; otherwise it pushes that bucket's href with that pathname's desk Find (`setDeskSearch`) set to the number. Esc returns focus to the toggle. On /incoming the list's STATUSES also sit top-left above the deliveries (`IncomingStatusChips`, ⌥1–⌥N) and write the same `?recon=`, narrowing the ledger AND the popout; with no list those chips are delivery-state buckets writing `?state=`. The sidebar shows no status rows.

NavSectionList.useWhen: page map rows, lane rows, pressable nav row, tactile nav block, sidebar row icon, lane door row, parent nav list, view glyph lookup (navRowGlyph)
NavSectionList.doNot: Do not render a page's own views with it — they live behind NavViewSwitcher. Do not light the current row with a per-row fill that blinks — one shared plate slides (layoutId). Do not put a count on NavItem.
NavSectionList.law: src/components/sidebar/contextual/NavSectionList.tsx + nav-block.ts. The PAGE MAP renderer (`?view=top`, and legacy pages): NAV_BLOCK_CLASS rows — flat at rest, lift on hover (card fill + hairline ring + shadow-sm), sink 1px on press — each led by its nav icon; a lane door opens the staffer's last view (useLaneDoorHref). Categories are split by a HAIRLINE (before/after each multi-row category), never a text heading; the name stays as the group's aria-label. `navRowGlyph(item, pageId)` is the one glyph lookup: a page's view gets its state glyph from nav-view-icons.ts (Exceptions amber AlertTriangle, Pick list violet PackageSearch), a map row its nav icon — shared with NavViewSwitcher and the ⌘K page map.

NavRecentsList.useWhen: sidebar recents, recent list, recently opened, recent sessions, chat threads, chat history list, session list in the sidebar, today yesterday groups, load more, show more, rename a thread, delete with undo, row menu in the sidebar, lit row for the open record, optimistic live row, recent chat hotkeys, alt digit chords, option 1 to open a chat
NavRecentsList.doNot: Do not build a per-page recents list (ChatSessionsNav is the drawer's legacy copy, not a pattern): every recents list is NavRecentsList driven by `NavContext.recents` + the surface registry. Do not put a text heading over a recency group — groups split by a hairline, the name is the list's aria-label. Do not hard-code a surface's verbs, events or endpoints in the component: declare `find`, `paged`, `rowActions`, `refreshOn`, `changedEvent` on the surface (src/lib/nav/recents/surfaces.ts). Do not route row verbs through /api/nav/recents — they write to the feed owner's route. No counts on rows.
NavRecentsList.law: src/components/sidebar/contextual/NavRecentsList.tsx + src/lib/nav/recents/{surfaces,live}.ts (operator 2026-09-27). Rows are NAV_BLOCK_CLASS h-8 blocks in local-calendar recency groups (groupByRecency: Today · Yesterday · Previous 7 days · Previous 30 days · Older) split by hairlines. ONE lit plate (NAV_BLOCK_PLATE_CLASS, layoutId) on the record the URL opens, else the page's live record (`usePublishNavLiveRecent` → `useNavLiveRecent`), which also sits on top until the feed lists it (each change of it refetches once). `find` → the page's Find text goes out as `q`; `paged` → 'Load more' follows the response's `nextBefore` (`GET /api/nav/recents?…&before=`). `rowActions` → hover ⋮ menu: Rename (inline field) · Delete (soft) with a 10s Undo toast = PATCH `{ restore: true }`, protocol PATCH `{ title }` / DELETE on `rowActions.endpoint` with `{id}`; success fires the surface's `changedEvent`, and its `refreshOn` events refetch the list. A row the feed has not listed carries no menu. `chords` → ⌥1…⌥9, ⌥0 (Alt on Windows / Linux, read from `code`) open the first ten painted rows from anywhere on the page, typing included; each row discloses its keycaps on hover / focus (HOTKEY FIRST, no room at rest).

DeskStageContext.useWhen: fullscreen, expand the table, stage state, is this table on a desk, desk stage, maximize the grid, floor view, industrial fullscreen, Cmd+Shift+F, in place or split
DeskStageContext.doNot: Do not add a second fullscreen state or a boolean beside it. The one state is a view enum — 'in-place' | 'split' | 'floor' (owner 2026-09-26) — with `fullscreen` DERIVED (view !== 'in-place'); set it with setView / toggleFloor, never a local flag. In place / Split are remembered per staffer per desk (`desk.<deskId>.view`); floor is a session posture, never stored, offered only while a list registers a floor face (useDeskFloorFace) and entered by ⌘/Ctrl+Shift+F or the Floor button DataTableFullscreenToggle paints beside ⤢. Floor = no page header / tabs / sidebar, the route's page ModeRegion flips to industrial (BRIEF §12 Mode D), records open in a fixed-width right rail beside an edge-to-edge list (owner 2026-09-27); Esc: record → check-set → floor → split. Its faces: DataTableFullscreenToggle on a table row (⤢ In place ↔ Split, Floor, Exit floor) and DeskRecordViewSwitch (In place / Split, hidden in floor) in the record header band that DeskRecordPlane paints in both views (operator 2026-09-26: the staffer chooses and can see which view they are in). DeskPageChrome OWNS the state and publishes it here; the control lives on the table's own toolbar row (DataTableFullscreenToggle), which renders NOTHING when useDeskStageOptional() is null — a station embed or a modal-hosted table has no stage to expand, and a dead control is worse than no control. Do not move the toggle up to the page header: in fullscreen that header is not rendered.
DeskStageContext.law: src/design-system/components/DeskStageContext.tsx. Operator 2026-08-30: the fullscreen control belongs on the table's row, not the page's.

DeskStageOverlay.useWhen: multi-field form on a desk, edit form over the table, inset form, row action form (release, revoke, unlink), config editor opened from a pencil, where does a form go, right rail or overlay
DeskStageOverlay.doNot: Do NOT mount this with fill="stage" to show a picked row's record: a record is placed by DeskRecordPlane, which drives this overlay for the in-place view and draws the fullscreen split itself. Do NOT put a multi-field form in the legacy right rail (DetailStackRailRegistrar / useRegisterRightPanel detail priority / a hand-rolled evidence aside). Use this directly for fill="inset" forms over the still-mounted table (Center Lock Q5): a row verb's form, or the editor behind a record's one-line config summary + pencil (org config that outlives the record — rules, roles — lives on a config page, never as record data). compound-row-chrome.useWhen: compound row height, select gutter width, edge rail width, gutter content inset, centre the check in the gutter, pin the check to the top, detail chevron band, fold hairline, fold close, group child rail, show a child row belongs to a group, multi-line PO grouping, soften the black line under a group
compound-row-chrome.doNot: Do not retype 48, 1.5rem, 3px or 2px anywhere — COMPOUND_ROW_PX, COMPOUND_SELECT_TRACK_REM, COMPOUND_EDGE_RAIL_CLASS, COMPOUND_GUTTER_RAIL_INSET_CLASS, COMPOUND_GUTTER_MARK_TOP_PIN_CLASS, COMPOUND_GUTTER_CHEVRON_BAND_CLASS, SLOT_TABLE_GROUP_CHILD_RAIL_CLASS and SLOT_TABLE_GROUP_FOLD_INNER_CLASS are the SoT and three consumers must agree (paint, full-bleed gutters, the virtualizer estimate). Gutter content — check, status glyph, chevron — reserves COMPOUND_GUTTER_RAIL_INSET_CLASS on EVERY row so the marks read as one centre line and the 3px rail never crowds them. The MARK (checklist square + resting status glyph) is pinned to the TOP through COMPOUND_GUTTER_MARK_TOP_PIN_CLASS — the 2026-09-04 `items-start pt-1` ruling STANDS and a 2026-09-15 pass that floated it to the row's middle was reverted by the operator ("the checklist icon should be pinned to the top and the drop-down icon should be below the checklist icon"). The detail / fold chevron goes in COMPOUND_GUTTER_CHEVRON_BAND_CLASS, the absolutely-positioned bottom half of the cell, so the mark plane stays the whole cell and the checkbox keeps its hit plane; never re-box the check inside a COMPOUND_TWO_LINE_CLASS track (that stack is for TEXT). GROUPING speaks with TWO soft marks and neither is black: MEMBERSHIP is SLOT_TABLE_GROUP_CHILD_RAIL_CLASS (2px `w-0.5 bg-border-default`, absolute on the IDENTITY track's leading edge, gated on `view.quietIdentity` in renderCompoundGridCell) and the CLOSE is SLOT_TABLE_GROUP_FOLD_INNER_CLASS (`h-px bg-border-default` on SlotTableGroupFold, both fold states). Never put the child rail in the select gutter — its first 3px are CompoundEdgeRail, which is per-row and conditional, so one 3px slot would mean "urgent" on one row and "child" on the next. Never restore bg-text-default on either mark (operator 2026-09-15 retired the black rule), never a 4-side envelope or inner box, never a second bar. Do not swap the inset for a spacing token — it is the rail's own measurement, used twice.
compound-row-chrome.law: src/components/tables/compound/compound-row-chrome.ts. SLOT_TABLE_PAINT_LAW.selectGutterStatus + leafDetailSelect. Operator 2026-09-15: "displayed centered in the middle" = the HORIZONTAL track (3px rail inset); the mark stays pinned to the top and the drop-down sits below it.

ProgressBar.useWhen: progress meter, completion bar, stage progress, percent done, N of M, goal against actual, segmented increments, Duolingo-style step bar, mobile-first step progress
ProgressBar.doNot: Do not animate width, height, or position — the fill is a scaleX transform with transformOrigin:'left' and w-full, gated by useReducedMotion. Law M1 bans layout tweens; transform was struck from that ban 2026-08-25, so the fill is legal only in that form. Duration is motionDuration.progressFill (100ms), never an inline literal. Progression is a COUNT, never a pointer position: pass satisfied-required-steps over total-required, so a pointer sitting on step 5 of 8 does not render 5/8. The `segments` prop is the touch/mobile-first face (operator 2026-09-14): N discrete increments, per-segment scaleX fill of the SAME law, aria progressbar wiring on the wrapper. Do not hand-roll a second segmented bar anywhere — kiosk, /m, or desk.
ProgressBar.law: docs/warehouse-os/PROGRESSION-INTERVIEW-LEDGER.md — PG12 (segmented squares + a scaleX fill; M1 stands unamended), PG6 (percent-done is a count, never a position), PD1 (this file's width tween was the violation). Operator 2026-09-14: PG12's segmented face is now real via `segments`.

StepProgressHeader.useWhen: step-flow header band, mobile-first wizard header, X close left + progress segments middle + n/N count right, kiosk pane form header, /m step flow header, Duolingo-style progress header
StepProgressHeader.doNot: Do not compose a step-flow header from a title band plus an inline meter — this band IS the header (operator 2026-09-14: 'all in one header, X top left, progress bar, one-out-of-ten top right'). Do not hand-roll the bar: it composes ProgressBar with `segments={total}`. The count counts COMPLETED units (PG6), never the index of the step in view. Do not add a pane title inside this band — the step eyebrow in the body names the current step. Back affordances inside a fixed-width form measure use this X when 'exit the flow' is the semantic; paged back-steps belong to the body, not this band.
StepProgressHeader.law: Operator 2026-09-14 — 'think Duolingo instead of text'; kiosk DS unification Phase 1. Composes ProgressBar (PG12/PG6/M1). Mounts: KioskRepairPane and KioskCartLedger, both via KioskPaneForm `progress`. Every mount's segment count is a gate table (repairStepGates, cartStepGates), never a step index.

ProcedureDeck.useWhen: station work surface, procedure steps, step column, work list, guided procedure, unbox steps, the surface an operator works a station from
ProcedureDeck.doNot: Do not gate capture on the active step. Evidence claims the step it belongs to, so the pointer is a HINT about what to capture next, never an authority that rejects input — scanning what step 5 wants while the pointer sits on step 2 satisfies step 5, and steps 3-4 stay open and unticked. Do not auto-complete the steps in between. Every step stays mounted from the first frame (existing invariant 1) — that is what makes a jumped-past open step visible without a scroll, so do not virtualize or collapse the list.
ProcedureDeck.law: docs/warehouse-os/PROGRESSION-INTERVIEW-LEDGER.md — PG6 (evidence claims its own step; progression is non-linear), PG3 (evidence advances the pointer).

StepStateBadge.useWhen: step state mark, procedure step box, done/skipped/pending mark, checklist square
StepStateBadge.doNot: Do not make it clickable and do not render a rounded-full dot. A step is evidence-derived — a square that clicks to tick reintroduces the banned hand-ticked checklist. `skipped` keeps the chevron and never the check: a skip is a recorded waiver that a person looked and moved past, not a claim the work happened, and a required step skipped this way carries a deviation reason. One mark serves both ProcedureChecklist and ProcedureDeck; do not fork it per view.
StepStateBadge.law: File docblock (shape + evidence-derived). docs/warehouse-os/PROGRESSION-INTERVIEW-LEDGER.md — PG3 (evidence advances; tick is the fallback), PG8 (a skipped required step is a recorded deviation), PG1 (one derivation at two altitudes).

calendar.useWhen: calendar, date picker, day picker, month grid, shadcn calendar, 21st.dev calendar, react-day-picker
calendar.doNot: Do not import 'react-day-picker/style.css'. This file names EVERY key in react-day-picker's UI enum, so no rdp-* class is emitted and the stylesheet is dead weight — while it was imported, the keys the old component missed (root, weeks, chevron) inherited library styling and .rdp-chevron{fill:var(--rdp-accent-color)} filled the nav chevron's stroked path into a solid blue triangle. Do not write data-[range-start=true] / data-[range-end=true] / data-[range-middle=true] chains: this repo is on react-day-picker v10, which emits none of those attributes — that is v9, and most shadcn range snippets in circulation are v9 or v8. Do not put raw text-blue-* inside an arbitrary variant ([&>button]: or hover:); the dark-scheme remap in styles/globals.css only rewrites the BARE class, so it goes dark-on-dark — use a themed token. Do not drop relative or w-fit from the root, and do not simplify nav to inset-x-0 top-0: the p-3 root makes those offsets wrong by 12px vertically and 16px horizontally. Range picking is calendar-range-select, not this with mode="range" hand-styled. A full field (trigger + popover + Apply) is DateRangePickerField or DateRangePickerPill, not this bare. Do not mount this as an inline table date editor. Slot-table ship-by / due date / pick a date in a cell is DateRangePickerField variant="compact" (not variant=range).
calendar.law: src/components/ui/calendar.tsx — shadcn/new-york lineage on react-day-picker v10, house tokens. Operator 2026-08-31: one calendar primitive; src/design-system/components/Calendar.tsx was deleted and all six consumers moved here.

calendar-range-select.useWhen: date range, range picker, from-to dates, period picker, week range, filter by date range, range calendar, start and end date
calendar-range-select.doNot: Do not hand-style a range on `calendar` — this file is the only place the range track is defined. range_middle must keep Tailwind's `!` suffix: in v10 a middle day is BOTH selected and range_middle and the two class strings land on the same cell, so equal specificity would let stylesheet order pick the winner. Do not move the endpoint pill off `selected` onto range_start/range_end — a half-picked range (from set, to open) sets only `selected`, because v10 requires both endpoints before it marks the range. Do not add a preset row above it; the four period chips were removed 2026-08-31 for restating the calendar and forcing the popover wider than the grid. This is the bare calendar — the trigger + popover + Apply field is DateRangePickerField variant="range", and the workbench-chrome pill is DateRangePickerPill. Do not drop this bare grid into a table cell. Cell / ship-by / due date is DateRangePickerField variant="compact".
calendar-range-select.law: src/components/ui/calendar-range-select.tsx — layers only range_start / range_end / range_middle over `calendar`. Operator 2026-08-31: ported from 21st.dev, retranslated from react-day-picker v9 to v10.

The URL is the state — search, filter, active tab and sort are controlled by the caller and parked in the URL. Do not mount FilterRefinementBar (or hunt tiles, or a second toolbar) above this table — DataTableFilterMenu always sits to the right of SearchField (DATA_TABLE_FILTER_IDLE when a family has no facets). Send through buildComposerReplyVars — never assemble SupportReplyVars by hand, or the station and the console drift on signing, emailCcs and photoIds again.

SearchResultRow.useWhen: search result row, find result, hit row, ranked result list, ⌘K result, /search results, browse hit, SearchResultRow
SearchResultRow.doNot: Do not fork this row — it is the ONE result row for the header preview, ⌘K, /search and every rail. Do not add a 3-dot (⋮) menu: click-to-select is the whole interaction and search rows carry zero row menus by design. Gate chrome on the `density` prop (compact | comfortable | dropdown), NEVER on a `md:`/`lg:` breakpoint — a desktop sidebar rail is narrow too, and a viewport query corrupts it. LAYOUT (operator 2026-09-12): the VERIFIABLE IDENTIFIER owns the leading column, because a warehouse reader scans top-to-bottom down the left edge. Do not seat a text-heavy status word (“UNASSIGNED”, “OPEN”) in that premier slot. Status is a minimal dot + concise badge sitting WITH the id, never a coloured dot on one edge of the row and its word on the other — that splits one fact across the full width and forces two fixations to read a single state. Do not repeat the entity noun (“Order”) under every title: it is the same on every row, so it is noise that costs a line which a real fact (qty, bin, exact stamp) should own. A relative stamp (“4d”) is not sufficient alone for SLA work — carry the exact timestamp with it. If a surface needs uniform columns, click-to-sort headers and operational fields, it wants the ONE TABLE ENGINE (DataTable), not a restyled list: a read plane is a MOUNT.
SearchResultRow.law: src/components/search/SearchResultRow.tsx — the single result row; SEARCH_RESULT_GRID owns its tracks. Operator 2026-09-12: id leads the row in monospace, status is a dot + badge beside it, the redundant entity label goes, and a loose list that wants columns becomes a DataTable mount. Operator 2026-09-25 (supersedes the DataTable-mount clause for /search): search is a find-and-identify job — its result list is fixed-width SearchResultRow rows and its record view is a search component (two-column record with "Open in desk"), never a remount of a desk table or ledger (DataTable, useCompoundSpreadsheet, OutboundOrdersLedger, OrderRecordView).

MobileShell.useWhen: phone shell, mobile shell, /m page frame, phone chrome, handheld frame, mobile top bar and drawer, phone column, mobile-first surface, phone page frame, RedesignedMobileShell

Exported as `RedesignedMobileShell`; the catalog id is the FILE. Do not add a bottom nav: the drawer replaced it (MobileSidebarDrawer.tsx), and reviving one needs an operator ruling, not a component. On lg+ the phone SoT stays a fixed phone-width column with thick gutters — never a stretched desk. No hover-only affordance anywhere on this surface; no raw palette class (semantic fills only). No route animation: a tap paints the next screen in the frame it is ready — never wrap `children` in AnimatePresence / a crossfade (operator 2026-09-25: "it shouldn't even display an animation at all").
MobileShell.law: src/components/mobile/redesign/MobileShell.tsx · docs/mobile-first/SURFACE_LAW.md §4/§7 · src/lib/mobile/mobile-first-surface.ts. Operator 2026-09-10: every operator verb must be completable on /m first.

MobileAccountFooter.doNot: No `border-t` — use elevationClass('raised','soft') for the lift. Staff bubble is StaffAvatar with avatarPhotoId={null} so the fill is staff.color_hex; never hash a name into a colour. The name rides a content inset (px-3 inner wrapper) while the ghost row stays edge-to-edge (px-0). min-h-11 touch floor. Two-line identity since 2026-09-15: name (leading-tight font-medium) with the signed-in email under it (text-role-micro text-text-soft, truncated, hidden when null) from session envelope user.email. The DESK twin (sidebar/master-nav/StaffAccountFooter) mirrors this row and popover but passes user.avatarPhotoId — the photo paints on the desk spine; the phone keeps the colour+initials bubble.

mobile-scan-cta.doNot: Scan has ONE door: the permanent top-right seat on every mobile screen. Do not add a drawer row, a bottom-nav tab, or a second in-page scan button — each is a second door to one destination. The kernel it opens is /m/scan; do not point it at a per-surface scan page.

MobilePhotoCountBadge.useWhen: photo count on a phone card, mobile photo badge, carton photo count, unbox photo count
MobilePhotoCountBadge.doNot: x0 is NEVER a door — no photos means no affordance, not a zero badge. Clamp negatives. Tabular figures so the count does not reflow the row. BottomSheet.useWhen: edit sheet from the /info pencil, hub dock verb form, confirmation sheet, picker sheet (choose a value, staff, reason, type), quick look at a linked item from inside another record (an item linked to a ticket), mobile sheet
BottomSheet.doNot: Never the PRIMARY record of the job being worked — an order while picking or packing, a carton, a unit, a bin, a SKU, a ticket. That is a full scrollable screen: the entity's hub on DetailHubScreen (/m/<entity>/[id]), opened as a route, with an X back to the job (MobileDetailTopBar close). A sheet is only for a quick look at a LINKED item from inside another record, an edit, a dock verb, a confirm or a picker. Lists on phone are flat hairline work rows — never rounded/elevated islands and never a DataTable as the phone SoT (SURFACE_LAW §5). Do not open a desk dialog or a RightRailHost detail.

DetailHubScreen.useWhen: mobile scanned entity hub, mobile record detail, phone drill-in, entity details and edit, phone record screen, scanned thing detail, repair hub, SKU exception hub, unit hub, bin hub, handling unit hub, receiving carton hub, order hub, scan-out hub, mobile exoskeleton, DetailRecordFrame, /info screen frame, job screen frame
DetailHubScreen.doNot: The hub is EDGE TO EDGE (operator 2026-09-25): no page padding and no gaps; card, ack, content and door rows run the full width, separated by one border-mode-rule; only text keeps its inset, and a content slot owns its own inset. Never wrap the slots in px-mode-page or space-y, and never box the card or the door list — full-bleed rows are what later left/right swipe actions attach to. This is the ONE record grammar on /m (the repair hub exoskeleton). Do not hand-roll a hub from ModeRegion + MobileDetailTopBar + cards: mount DetailHubScreen with card = a DetailSummaryCard mapper (whole card → /info), rows = detailDoor(base, id, title, icon, { meta, enabled }) doors from @/lib/mobile/detail-door, dock = DetailDock (≤3 verbs, one primary) — or MobileCaptureWindow when the hub's job is scanning, and put the dock's sheets in children. /info and each job screen mount DetailRecordFrame. Never put a heading above the card, an Edit button or pencil on the hub (the only edit is the /info bar pencil opening a BottomSheet), router.back()/router.push for Back (backHref), a nested <main>, useEffect+fetch for hub facets (React Query, qk.<entity>.hub), a hand-rolled sticky bottom bar, or MobileTriagePage / ItemCardRow / a row → BottomSheet as an entity record. A new hub route goes into DETAIL_HUB_PEERS; porting one drops DETAIL_HUB_UNPORTED_BASELINE.
DetailHubScreen.law: src/design-system/components/DetailHubScreen.tsx · docs/handoff/mobile-ds-law-exoskeleton-HANDOFF.md. Operator 2026-09-24: one grammar for every scanned thing — a compact information display on top, then grouped into exact actions (photos, …) below; delete the old mobile display rules rather than keep them beside it.

DetailSummaryCard.useWhen: hub summary card, card slot of DetailHubScreen, compact entity card, read-only record preview, scan detail summary, repair hub card, unit hub card, SKU exception card
DetailSummaryCard.doNot: Full-bleed, no border box and no radius (operator 2026-09-25: edge to edge); the hub draws the rule under it. This is the first, read-only preview of ONE scanned entity — never a dashboard tile, a list-row replacement, or a second editable form. Exactly one full-width title (truncate), at most two job-relevant caption lines, a mono identifier bottom-left and one status chip bottom-right. The ID and chip MUST share box height (transparent border + py-0.5 on the ID; border + py-0.5 on the chip). The WHOLE card opens the entity's /info screen; do not put a pencil, Edit text, status selector, or another button on the card. The ONLY edit pencil is in the /info top bar. Do not put a heading such as Information above the card. It fills the card slot of DetailHubScreen (map an entity onto it, e.g. RepairInfoCard); the hub, not the card, mounts DetailNav doors and the <=3-verb DetailDock. Pick and pack hubs open their existing task runner rather than embedding its steps.
DetailSummaryCard.law: src/design-system/components/DetailSummaryCard.tsx · docs/handoff/mobile-entity-exoskeleton-HANDOFF.md. Operator 2026-09-24: simple first view; details on tap; status bottom-right; customer phone in the preview; pencil only in the expanded view.

DetailDock.useWhen: mobile entity hub verbs, hub dock, thumb-zone verbs, bottom action dock, edge-to-edge bottom bar, flush verb bar, repair hub actions, SKU exception actions, scanned entity verbs, mobile exoskeleton dock, scan dock, serial scan bottom, scan button, job CTA bar, next unit bar, selection bar, batch action bar, single full-width bottom button, inline verb band, row verbs, take and pass buttons, board row actions, order card actions, 2x2 action grid under a record, scan in the middle of the bottom bar, centred scan button
DetailDock.doNot: At most three verbs and exactly one primary. The bar is FLUSH (operator 2026-09-25: "no padded top, left and right for the buttons, must be edge to edge"): verbs fill the bar edge to edge with square corners and no gap, a 1px border-mode-rule between adjacent verbs, only the safe-area inset below — never wrap it in page padding, re-add a grid gap, or pass rounded-mode to its cells. It is the ONLY surface on a hub that changes the entity: never add verbs to the summary card, the top bar, or the door rows. Do not hand-roll a sticky bottom nav with a Button grid on a hub; that is this component. It is also every phone screen's bottom execution bar (operator 2026-09-25, industrial terminal block): 72px flush cells (min-h-18), instant ink inversion on press (no transition, no scale), a leading-edge 500ms lock so a double-tap fires once, and a press buzz where the Vibration API exists. State 3 — a one-job screen (Next unit, Scan another label) passes ONE verb and it fills the bar; State 2 — a selection passes selection={{ count, onClear }} and a dark 30% dismiss cell (✕ N SEL) leads ≤2 verbs. Never hand-roll a sticky bottom bar for a job CTA or a selection bar; never bring global navigation to the bottom (it lives in MobileSidebarDrawer). Scanning is NOT a dock verb: a screen whose job is scanning (serials into a visit, labels into a queue) mounts MobileCaptureWindow (src/components/mobile/station/MobileCaptureWindow.tsx) as its bottom surface — lens, collapsed Scan bar to re-arm, and its keyed fallback for typing a code by hand — or it has no scan at all. Never a Scan verb that opens the window, never a hand-rolled typed-entry bar beside it (operator 2026-09-25). A verb that NAVIGATES to /m/scan ("Scan again") is not a scanner and stays a verb. INLINE (owner 2026-09-26, pick edge-to-edge): placement="inline" is the same band in-flow under a record (a list row, an order card) — full width with a border-t rule, not sticky, no safe-area pad, up to four verbs (four = flush 2×2, 1px rules both ways), 48px cells whose labels wrap and never truncate. Never hand-roll a padded grid-cols-2 gap-2 of bordered Buttons under a row; that is this. CENTRED SCAN (owner 2026-09-26): on a scanning job screen the camera's collapsed Scan bar is the dock's MIDDLE cell between two verbs, in its success fill for hierarchy — pass it via MobileCaptureWindow collapsedFrame={(scan) => <DetailDock center={scan} …/>}; never a Scan row stacked above the dock, and never a Scan verb of your own. With the lens up, the dock renders alone under the panel.
DetailDock.law: src/design-system/components/DetailDock.tsx · docs/handoff/mobile-entity-exoskeleton-HANDOFF.md (DetailDock, from RepairWorkbenchDock) · docs/handoff/fnsku-reprint-HANDOFF.md (flush bar). Operator 2026-09-24: repair hub is the reference for every scanned entity. · docs/design-system/HANDOFF-pick-edge-to-edge.md (inline placement).

KioskPaneForm.useWhen: kiosk centre pane frame, kiosk pane shell, counter tablet pane column, kiosk step flow frame, kiosk repair/cart pane, kiosk action floor
KioskPaneForm.doNot: There is NO title face, and adding one re-opens the double-band bug (two stacked chromes on pickup, 2026-09-14). `progress` present → this pane owns its header and it IS StepProgressHeader; `progress` absent → the SHELL painted the header and the pane paints nothing. Never reach back for KIOSK_PANE_HEADER_BAND / KIOSK_PANE_HEADER_TITLE inside a pane, and never re-grow a `hideHeader` flag. The footer hairline is DERIVED from `progress` (step flows float their key, shell-titled panes carry the floor band) — never a per-pane knob. Do not hand-roll `flex h-full flex-col` → `overflow-y-auto` → footer row; that is this frame, and re-assembling it is how the repair footer lost its hairline. `hero` REPLACES the scroll body for a done/empty face; it is never a third band.
KioskPaneForm.law: src/components/kiosk/KioskPaneForm.tsx + kiosk-pane-frame.test.ts (4 contracts). Kiosk DS unification Phase 1, 2026-09-14. Mounts: KioskRepairPane, KioskCartLedger (cart ported 2026-09-15 with `progress`), KioskCartDoneFace. Buyback/Pickup panes deleted 2026-09-23.

KioskChip.useWhen: kiosk chip, counter tablet pill, touch chip, selectable reason pill, fact chip on a kiosk card, kiosk cart line facts, rounded pill for a tablet
KioskChip.doNot: Do not use the desk `badge` on a kiosk surface — it is square (rounded-none), 18px tall and bordered for dense grid rows, and overriding its radius per call site is the fork this component exists to stop. Do not hand-compose KIOSK_PILL + a tone token (ReasonSelector was doing exactly that), and never hand-roll `rounded-full` + padding. Two faces only: `row` = full-width selectable pill with aria-pressed, `meta` = inline fact chip on a card. KioskChip.law: src/components/kiosk/KioskChip.tsx + kiosk-chip-family.test.ts (5 contracts). KioskCartLineCard.useWhen: kiosk cart line, cart line row, counter tablet cart list item, kiosk cart card, customer-facing cart line
KioskCartLineCard.doNot: A cart line is a CARD, never a CompoundRow / DataTable — SURFACE_LAW §5: lists on a phone-shaped surface are cards. Operator 2026-09-14 on the compound-table cart: 'this is a wrong display'. Zero [data-grid-row] and zero role=table in the cart. The card is FLAT: it sits on the flat KIOSK_UTILITY_SHEET, so separation is `border-border-hairline` + MOBILE_SCAN_ROW_CORNER, never elevationClass — a shadow inside a sheet the operator already de-shadowed is the same popover cue one altitude down (2026-09-15). The card IS the edit affordance (tap to correct); void stays the swipe verb on KioskCartSwipeRow. Staff and customer faces mount the SAME card — `readOnly` drops the interaction, not the anatomy. Facts ride KioskChip meta chips derived by cartLineCardView; do not re-derive a line's amount or state label in a caller.
KioskCartLineCard.law: src/components/kiosk/KioskCartLineCard.tsx · src/lib/kiosk/cart-card-view.ts · docs/mobile-first/SURFACE_LAW.md §5. Kiosk DS unification Phase 2, 2026-09-14; flattened 2026-09-15 with the sheet.

KioskTicketStep.useWhen: kiosk support ticket choice, link existing ticket on a tablet, create new ticket at the counter, attach a repair drop-off to a helpdesk ticket, kiosk ticket picker, counter ticket candidate list, create-or-link slider under a signature
KioskTicketStep.doNot: NOT its own step, not mounted flat, and not a stacked pill pair. It rides UNDER the signature pad inside Review & sign, revealed by the ink: operator 2026-09-15 asked for it 'after the customer has submitted their signature', then collapsed the fifth step ('because the stepper is full at that review and sign step, would it be best to include a slider … below the signature so it would be mounted under one step?'), then simplified the control ('the create new and the link existing should be simplified into just one slider where you would be able to slide back and forth since this would be on a mobile display, and automatically select create new ticket'). So: ONE sunken pill TRACK holding two KioskChip row halves — the selected half's accent wash is the thumb, the idle half stays transparent because the track is the only sunken plane. CREATE is the position an untouched control shows, which is honest only because `null` also posts as create (kioskTicketWork) and counts as settled (isKioskTicketChoiceSettled); the HALF-FINISHED state — slid to Link with nothing picked — is what still refuses the commit. Do not mount the DESK link surface: TicketPicker / TicketPickRow / DenseComposeSearchInput / SearchableSelectField (ClaimModeSelect) are desk-micro chrome built for a mouse, and a candidate list on a counter tablet is CARDS (SURFACE_LAW §5), the KioskCartLineCard anatomy — hairline + MOBILE_SCAN_ROW_CORNER, title line, facts as KioskChip meta chips. Do not re-implement the search: the debounce / abort / error-mapping / stale-result rules are the shared useTicketSearch, adapted by useKioskTicketSearch (URL + kioskFetchHealed transport are the ONLY kiosk-specific parts) — the same split useClaimTicketSearch made for a carton. The decision is a VISIT fact on the session root (`ticketChoice`), never a cart-line payload field: `ticketWork` is transaction-level and fans out to one outbox row per repair. A picked ticket outlives a re-search (the hook's own `selectedTicket` is unused here) and outranks the ticket-number PROJECTION on the paperwork, because ATTACH_TICKET stamps repair_service.ticket_number with it.
KioskTicketStep.law: src/components/kiosk/KioskTicketStep.tsx · src/components/kiosk/useKioskTicketSearch.ts · src/lib/kiosk/repair-ticket-choice.ts · GET /api/kiosk/repair/ticket-candidates · kiosk-ticket-step.test.ts (7 contracts) + repair-ticket-choice.test.ts (7 behaviours). Operator 2026-09-15. Mounted under the SignaturePad on KioskRepairPane's Review & sign (step 4 of 4); a settled answer is half of repairStepGates[3], the other half being the signature. That step's floor commits with ONE orange key — Button variant="warning" + KIOSK_POS_CTA, 'Submit repair' — and its heading row carries the labelled Print CTA on the right.

KioskCustomerIntake.useWhen: kiosk customer intake, capture customer name phone email address, counter tablet customer block
KioskCustomerIntake.doNot: ONE intake face across every kiosk channel (repair · buyback · pickup · cart) — do not write a second name/phone/email block. `fields` picks which of the four are asked; `entry` switches the control to the KIOSK_POS_ENTRY face. The form control is KioskEntryField (`src/components/kiosk/KioskEntryField.tsx`), never a raw <input> and never the desk field primitives: KIOSK_POS_ENTRY holds the 16px floor that stops iOS from zooming the whole surface on focus (COUNTER_MIN_FIELD_TEXT_PX). Phone is the MATCH KEY — it is the only blocking customer field (visit-triage `target: 'customer'`); name, email and address are warnings and must not gate a step or a submit.
KioskCustomerIntake.law: src/components/kiosk/KioskCustomerIntake.tsx + KioskCustomerIntake.test.ts · src/lib/kiosk/visit-triage.ts. Operator: 'intake their information like name, email address, phone number, address'.

KioskEntryField.useWhen: kiosk entry field, kiosk form field, kiosk text input, placeholder-in-box input on a tablet, kiosk notes textarea, signer name on a kiosk-face sign-off, desk pickup signer / decline reason field
KioskEntryField.doNot: Never a raw <input>/<textarea> and never the desk field primitives on a kiosk-face flow: every input answers to KIOSK_POS_ENTRY / KIOSK_POS_ENTRY_AREA (16px floor — no iOS focus zoom). No floating label; the placeholder is the prompt and the sr-only <label> is the accessible name. Pass `idScope` whenever the same `name` repeats on one screen. StaffChoiceRowButton.doNot: The row IS the card — rounded-xl border, its own surface; never wrap it in a second card and never inset it in a parent outline. EvidenceDisclosure.doNot: Do not hand-roll a <details> fact or section beside these — EvidenceFactRow (label · value), EvidenceFactDisclosure (label · value · +/−, expands in place) and EvidenceDisclosure (label · summary · +/−) own the w-24 label lane and the trailing cell. Every right-edge glyph of a record row or evidence fact (+/−, open ↗, edit ✎, the price Items chevron) sits in RECORD_TRAILING_CELL_CLASS — one 32px cell flush with the content edge, 14px glyph centred — so they stack on one vertical axis. A glyph drawn INSIDE another control (SearchableSelectField ⌄) lands on that axis with RECORD_TRAILING_GLYPH_INSET_CLASS, never its own pr-*/mr-*/ml-auto. Never repeat the summary/value inside the expanded body. The triage stack (RecordEvidence's EvidenceSection / EvidenceFact) is the non-disclosing sibling — do not mix the two in one column.
EvidenceDisclosure.law: src/design-system/components/record-ledger/EvidenceDisclosure.tsx + src/design-system/tokens/industrial-record.ts (RECORD_TRAILING_CELL_CLASS, RECORD_TRAILING_GLYPH_INSET_CLASS). AnchoredLayer.useWhen: dropdown panel, anchored popout, bulk list popout, tracking numbers list, row menu with actions, menu under a trigger, header menu, L2 disclosure layer, progressive disclosure popover
AnchoredLayer.doNot: Do not read facts in a popout and act on them somewhere else: every row's verbs (Edit ✎, Copy, ✕ delete) sit INLINE in that row, on the RECORD_TRAILING_CELL_CLASS axis (Principle 3 — action proximity). Do not navigate the page or replace the list to show this layer — it floats over a frame that stays put (Principle 2 — stable frame). Do not trap focus here (only L4 dialogs trap). Do not hard-code a corner on the panel: it follows the mode (rounded-mode-control) — square on the Floor, rounded in triage. Do not hand-roll a portal + outside-click + Esc: mount this (or the house Popover that wraps it).
AnchoredLayer.law: src/design-system/primitives/AnchoredLayer.tsx (house Popover wraps it). Disclosure ladder: DESIGN_SYSTEM.md. This primitive is L2. Esc closes (useEscapeClose) and, when the close dropped focus, focus returns to the element that opened the layer — a click that moved focus elsewhere, or a combobox input that kept it, is left alone.
